text: JSON is the universal language for exchanging data between programs, websites, and APIs.
The json module converts between Python objects and JSON text in both directions.
dumps turns a Python dictionary into a JSON string, and indent makes it neatly readable.
[chuckle] Notice how the structure maps cleanly — dictionaries become objects, lists stay lists.
[sniff] loads does the reverse, parsing a JSON string back into real Python objects you can use.
So the parsed result behaves like a normal dictionary, and you index into it as usual.
[sigh] A full round-trip — dump then load — preserves your data exactly, proving the conversion is faithful.
There are also dump and load, which write to and read from files directly.
[groan] Any time your program talks to the web or saves settings, JSON is almost certainly how the data travels.
